text:
liyu: FYI while smoke testing newbridge (q4_0) on canary I hit a reproducible detok mismatch for mixed CJK+latin numeric lines. Small run shows chrF dropping and some translations inserting spaces inside numbers.
marta: can you paste a minimal repro example? Is it tokenization (preproc) or model output shift?
liyu: input: \"北京市 2021 年度报告（摘要）\"
liyu: baseline detok: 北京市 2021 年度报告（摘要）
liyu: q4_0+kvcache detok: 北京市 2021 年度 报告（摘要）  <-- extra space before 报告
liyu: noticed similar for ja+hangul mixtures where ZWJ disappears between kana+hangul clusters.
ron: weird. that spacing looks like a token boundary moved to split a CJK token before the word. Can you show token ids?
liyu: baseline ids (slice): [1102, 5533, 90021, 77]  // shows 90021 covers '2021 年度'
liyu: q4_0+kvcache ids:    [1102, 5533, 900, 21, 77]  // split into 900 + 21 -> space produced in detok
marta: splitting numbers into two tokens would change KV cache offsets during generation. Does this happen only with kvcache enabled?
liyu: yes, I toggled kvcache=false and the split disappears. So seems interaction with chunked cache path.
infra-bot: infra note: canary runtime uses kernel set \"fast-kv-v2\" for q4_0 on A100-80G as of build 2024-11-02.
ron: did we bump tokenizer lib in the model bundle? That could change merges in borderline cases.
liyu: tokenizer in bundle is unchanged, but the runtime does apply a normalization step for batched tokenize that was recently refactored (PR 4021). Possible regression there.
marta: propose triage steps: 1) run model w/old tokenize path + q4_0+kvcache 2) new tokenize path + baseline float weights 3) q4_0 with old kernel (fast-kv-v1). That isolates preproc vs quant vs kernel.
liyu: starting 1 & 3 on canary now.
eval-bot: running targeted eval: 1200 mixed CJK samples; compare newbridge q4_0+kvcache vs float-baseline
eval-bot: overall chrF delta = -1.9, BLEU delta = -2.4
eval-bot: subsegment: numeric+paren group delta BLEU = -6.1 (p<0.001), ja/ko mixed scripts delta chrF = -4.8
ron: those deltas are concentrated; sounds like token boundary jitter leading to deterministic detok differences plus downstream generation changes. Any RTL issues observed?
liyu: we saw one class of en->ar samples where opening/closing bracket orientation flipped when punctuation followed a non-latin token (e.g., \"اسم (2020)\" -> \"اسم )2020(\"). Suspect bidi handling edge-case during prefix caching.
marta: can you run the bidi-oriented unit tests and the ZWJ preservation tests with kvcache chunking on/off?
liyu: running them now. quick grep shows failing cases only when batch_size>1 and kvcache.chunksize>=64. Single-token generation paths pass.
liyu: quick inspect of the refactor PR shows we moved normalization after batching to reduce CPU time; maybe it should run per-example.
ron: ok let's revert that normalization change on the canary runtime and re-run the evals. If revert fixes, we can patch to move normalization earlier or make it stable w.r.t batching.
liyu: revert applied to canary runtime tag newbridge-rc-17r; re-running eval-bot for the 1200 sample suite.
eval-bot: rerun complete: chrF delta now -0.2, BLEU delta -0.1, numeric subgroup delta = -0.3
marta: excellent. sounds like a preprocessing ordering bug. Can we add a unit test that exercises CJK+number token boundaries with batching and kvcache chunking?
ron: on it, I'll add tests to tokenization-suite and a regression check in the CI gating the runtime refactor.
liyu: filing a follow-up FR: prefer deterministic per-example normalization before batching. I'll attach failing inputs and the quick repro script: 
```
# repro tokenize split
python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from model_preproc import tokenize_batch
s = '北京市 2021 年度报告（摘要）'
# emulate batched path
print('batched tokens:', tokenize_batch([s, s], normalize_after_batch=True))
print('per-example tokens:', tokenize_batch([s, s], normalize_after_batch=False))
PY
```
liyu: tagging @infra for kernel review and @devexp to update onboarding notes about kvcache caveats.
ron: thanks all. hold release until we confirm stable on the canary for ja/ko/zh and RTL bracket tests. :white_check_mark:
